data.name: Aftar
data.gender_notes: Aftar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: The one who brings good news
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Aftar means 'the one who brings good news.' This name is derived from the Arabic verb 'aftara,' which means 'to bring good news.' In Islamic history, Prophet Sulaiman (Solomon) is known to have had a servant named Aftar who brought him good news from various parts of his kingdom. The name Aftar carries the meaning “The one who brings good news” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aftar usually hope their child will grow to embody the one who brings good news and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Bringing peace and joy through good news
data.etymology: Aftar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “The one who brings good news.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aftar total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_arabic.name: أفتر
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من الفعل افترى، بمعنى اتهم أو ظلم
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم ذو أصول عربية، مشتق من الفعل افترى الذي يعني اتهم أو ظلم. يعتبر الافتراء في الإسلام من الأخلاق الذميمة، حيث يحث القرآن على تجنبها وعدم اتهام الناس ظلماً. يستخدم الاسم في بعض الأحيان لتعبر عن الشخص الذي يتهم الآخرين ظلماً أو يفتري عليهم.

in_urdu.name: افتر
in_urdu.meaning: مطلب ہے ظلم یا کسی پر غلط الزام لگانا
in_urdu.long_meaning: افتر نام عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے ظلم کرنا یا کسی پر غلط الزام لگانا۔ یہ نام اسلامی تقویم میں ان افراد کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو ظلم و ستم سے دور رہتے ہیں اور راستباز ہیں۔ اس نام کا استعمال جنوبی ایشیاء میں مسلمانوں کے ذریعہ کیا جاتا ہے، خاص طور پر پاکستان اور بھارت میں۔

in_hindi.name: अफ्तार
in_hindi.meaning: अफतार का अर्थ है झूठा आरोप या अन्याय
in_hindi.long_meaning: अफतार एक अरबी नाम है जिसका अर्थ है झूठा आरोप लगाना या अन्याय करना। इस्लामी परंपरा में, यह नाम उन लोगों के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है जो झूठ और अन्याय से दूर रहते हैं। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम अक्सर उन बच्चों को दिया जाता है जो सच्चाई और न्याय के साथ जीना सीखते हैं।

in_pashto.name: افټر
in_pashto.meaning: د ظلم یا غلط تور لګولو معنی
in_pashto.long_meaning: افټر نوم د عربي ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې د ظلم یا غلط تور لګولو معنی لري. په اسلامي کلتور کې، دا نوم د هغو کسانو لپاره کارول کیږي چې د ظلم او ستم څخه لیرې پاتې دي او د حق او عدالت په لاره روان دي. په افغانستان او پاکستان کې، دا نوم ډیری وختونه د هغو ځوانانو لپاره غوره کیږي چې د صداقت او انصاف سره ژوند کوي.

in_english.name: Aftar
in_english.meaning: Derived from Arabic, meaning accusation or injustice
in_english.long_meaning: The name Aftar originates from Arabic roots, specifically from the verb 'aftara,' which means to accuse falsely or to do injustice. In Islamic tradition, the name signifies a person who is just and avoids false accusations. Etymologically, it relates to the Quranic emphasis on justice and truthfulness. Historically, the name has been used across various Muslim cultures to denote individuals known for their fairness and integrity.

historical_references.reference: After the Battle of Badr (624 CE), the Muslims were faced with a food shortage. The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) sent a small group of men, led by Mus'ab ibn Umair, to the tribe of Thaqif to invite them to Islam. The Thaqif, who were traditionally allies of the Meccans, were initially reluctant to join the Muslims. However, when they heard that the Muslims were out of provisions and in dire need of food, they decided to help them out of humanitarian concerns. The Muslims were thus able to sustain themselves until their next crop harvest. This event came to be known as 'Aftar' or 'The Banquet'.
historical_references.context: Islamic history, Battle of Badr, Food shortage, Invitation to Islam, Thaqif tribe

historical_references.reference: Aftar is also the name of the sixth month in the Islamic calendar, which marks the end of Ramadan and the beginning of Shawwal. It is a time of celebration and thanksgiving, marking the completion of the obligatory fasting during Ramadan. The name 'Aftar' comes from the Arabic word for 'breaking the fast'.
historical_references.time_period: Varies annually, based on lunar calendar
historical_references.context: Islamic calendar, Month of Shawwal, End of Ramadan, Fasting, Celebration

modern_usage.modern_context: The Islamic month of Ramadan, a period of fasting from sunrise to sunset, is a time of spiritual reflection, increased devotion, and heightened community spirit. The breaking of the fast, known as 'Aftar', has evolved into a socially significant event. People welcome the evening by sharing meals with their families and friends at home or attending community Iftar parties in mosques, community centres, or Iftar tents set up in open spaces. Social media platforms like Instagram, Twitter, and Facebook are used to share Iftar experiences, recipes, and photos of Iftar meals from around the world. Additionally, food drives and charitable initiatives during Ramadan have become increasingly popular, with many communities coming together to provide meals for those in need.
